title: Waymo Robotaxis Pulled From Freeways Indefinitely - Slashdot

content_html:
Waymo has temporarily suspended freeway operations across all its robotaxi markets after California regulators ordered the company off the state's highways over repeated incidents involving construction zones. The restriction follows a June recall (PDF) of nearly 3,800 vehicles and subsequent software updates (PDF) that failed to prevent further incidents, including a robotaxi driving past a California Highway Patrol rolling roadblock. Ars Technica reports: "Safety is at the foundation of everything we do," Waymo told Ars. "Following recent freeway construction zone encounters on U.S. 101 in California that did not involve any injuries or collisions, the California DMV has implemented an operating restriction on freeway operations in the state. In alignment with our safety-first principles, we have also temporarily restricted freeway operations across our other operating markets to evaluate our performance. Our ride-hailing service continues to operate safely on surface streets, serving over half a million trips each week. We are working with the California DMV and other state officials diligently and responsibly to resume freeway operations."

Waymo also told Ars it was continuing to work with the various California agencies that regulate transport. Until the suspension, Waymo was only conducting highway operations in Los Angeles and the Bay Area in California, as well as in Arizona.
